closed comparison collar around the chi=1 plateau, inside the same local type
and away from every other control support. For points at the plateau edge,
the comparison slab may leave chi=1 but must remain within this collar; the
collar's bounded bump derivatives give the same local estimate. On slabs of
length 4 log(1/eta_m(t_nu)), the sharper finite-frame residual is
 r_{n,m}(t)=O_n((eta_m(t)+t^(-3/2))(1+log(1/eta_m(t)))+eta_m(t)^2).
For fixed m, this divided by eta_m^(3/4) tends to zero. The graph correction is
bounded by C_n Omega_n(t) t^(-9/16). Dividing it by the desired eta_m^(3/4)
multiplies Omega_n by D_m^(3/4). Put a_nu=eta_m(t_nu)^(3/4). Finite-cluster
Taylor expansion and finite-matrix inversion therefore give the ENTIRE local
matrix expansion
 E_j^(n)=a_nu z_nu B_n(s(j),b(j))
          +O_n(a_nu^2+r_{n,m}(j)+Omega_n(j)j^(-9/16)).
This is a bound in full p_n-by-p_n matrix norm. The matrix B_n has uniformly
bounded norm over the finitely many band-n crossing types and b near a, and
its chosen off-diagonal entry has the source's fixed nonzero sign. Choose T_m
so that r_{n,m}/a_nu and D_m^(3/4)Omega_n are smaller than any prescribed band-n
fraction, simultaneously for n<=m and all later applicable times in that stage.

entry has its signed leading term uniformly over all other controls. The entire
local norm bound is needed for Step 7; a bound only for the selected entry does
not suffice.

ARGUMENT-EXPOSED RED-TEAM AUDIT
Uniform fixed-cutoff transfer for the proposed common metric
2026-10-08. No other auditor reports read. No descendants used.

VERDICT

The narrow uniform analytic transfer mechanism is valid under the explicit
hypotheses below. I found no circular dependence of its operator modulus on
future stage start times. Its proof does not require an effective rate for the
modulus, nor any estimate uniform in the cutoff n.

Two auxiliary estimates must be made explicit in PROOF_v2:

(a) D_m must dominate phase SECOND derivatives of the controlled links, as well
as the first derivatives of links, low frames, and bump data. One can choose this
before radial scheduling. Admissible schedules must first satisfy a weak bound
D_m S_m T_m^(-1/4) <= 1/2, which compares a bump center's time with every time in
its support. The stronger averaging start condition already permits this.

(b) On an own-band crossing plateau, the ENTIRE finite matrix error must be
O_n(eta_m(t_nu)^(3/4)), with a constant independent of m. A signed estimate only
for its chosen entry and the global O_n(t^(-9/16)) matrix bound do not justify a
fixed column radius rho_n when D_m grows. The local freezing proof and the same
stage suppression of the graph term give the needed entire-matrix estimate.
An exact algebraic counterexample to the weaker inference is recorded below.

These are fillable analytic details, not counterexamples to the proposed
metric. This audit does not validate the C-infinity angular skeleton in Step 1,
its path-space density claims, the pinned manuscript's spectral constructions,
the entire countable matching construction, or the complete common-metric
theorem. Those remain separate dependencies. Conditional on the skeleton and
its protected gaps, Steps 3-5 can be stated rigorously without future-schedule
circularity. The all-radius growth passage also introduces no new uniformity
problem once the exact lines and their spherical growth bounds exist.

SOURCE AND READ DEPTH
